reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item with the same correct numbers (about 35,294 GEL profit tax plus 10,000 GEL withholding) and give the same correct conclusions. B describes the deemed-distribution rules more accurately, since it names loans to individuals as a taxable object. It also describes the over-cap consequence of the small business regime more accurately, and it adds useful next steps such as getting the bookkeeper's written basis and the refund risk. A says the 3% rate applies only to the excess over the cap, which is less accurate, and its article and chapter references are looser.

A: States the higher ~3% small-business rate applies only to the excess over the 500,000 GEL cap; it applies to income from the point of exceedance, not just the excess.
